doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Olatunji phone call, a Nipsie Russell joke and jazz jokes
summary: A misdirected insult on the phone and a baboon-on-the-moon routine; he won't share his blue jokes.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Tell me about Joseph Casavubu and Patrice Lamumba.

Years ago there was a trumpet player by the name of Nick Travis. He used to – we used to call each other Deedle-ee and Nicholai and stuff like that. One time, a cat named Olatunji, a bass – a conga player, called – let’s see. How – I don’t remember how this actually went down. But he called – I don’t know how it was, but he insulted . . .
. . . Olatunji, because he [Travis] thought it was me [Terry] calling or something, and he [Travis] came on with this title, and he really insulted the heck out of Olatunji.
It was a private joke, and you . . .

Yeah, right. That made me think of that first. But the Lamumba – Nipsie Russell had a bit that he used to use, where he said, during the race for the nuclear physics thing, they had a program going on in Africa where they were going to put something in space. So the Africans were working on a project to put a baboon on the moon. He said you could fly low over this country, and all you could hear was a drum beat, “bing a boom, bing a boom,” and everybody’s humming, saying, “A baboon on the moon by June. A baboon on the moon.” The nuclear physicist who was the head of the program, he was a descendent of Casavoubu and Mabutu, and his name was Sackodudu. “A baboon on the moon.” But I thought about that Olatunji thing first, because Olatunji was mad, man. He was angry.
Was Olatunji trying to reach you?

I think – I don’t know how – I was on – I don’t know how that phone call came about. Nick was calling – it might have been, maybe Nick might have – Olatunji might have called Nick for a date, because we used a big band. Nick was a great trumpet player, and I did almost all of Tunji’s dates. Nick might have been on one of them. So he might have been calling him about the date, and Nick thought it was me, and he came on with this stuff. I imagine it was very insulting, almost like someone using the “n” word.
Tell me. You’ve got a lot of jokes, but do you have any favorite jazz jokes or – yeah, jazz jokes?
To tell you the truth, Bill, I don’t really know, because most of the stuff I get into is kind of blue anyhow. It might not be too fitting for a history of this sort. So, I don’t know.
